textos.A maioria dos que recomendam destaca o d: Most of those who recommend the film highlight Denzel Washington's performance. In contrast, most of those who do not recommend it point to a confusing, disjointed narrative, and also criticize the slowness of the pace and the long running time of the production.

textos.Mesmo entre as críticas negativas, muito: Even among the negative reviews, many acknowledge that Denzel Washington delivers a strong, charismatic performance, often being the highlight of the film.

textos.Dirigido por Spike Lee e lançado em 1992: Directed by Spike Lee and released in 1992, Malcolm X is a historical and biographical drama with a running time of 202 minutes. The film portrays the trajectory of Malcolm X, leader of the American Black movement Nation of Islam, covering the most striking periods of his personal life and political activism.
textos.A experiência cinematográfica é caracter: The cinematic experience is characterized by a long-running narrative that unfolds at a measured pace. The work relies on a detailed historical setting to follow the protagonist's transformations through different phases.
textos.Na grande maioria das notas (~90%), a re: Among the vast majority of ratings (~90%), the reaction is overwhelmingly favorable. Most praise Denzel Washington's performance as the main element of the work. Beyond that, a good portion comment on the long running time and the pace adopted, while a considerable number devote praise to Spike Lee's direction.
textos.Para quem assume uma postura intermediár: For those taking a middling stance, in a minimal fraction of the ratings (~8%), about half single out the excessive running time and the slow pace as problematic aspects of the viewing. Despite these reservations, many acknowledge Denzel Washington's performance, while a significant share question the way Malcolm X's portrayal and politics were presented.
textos.Sob o olhar do grupo mais insatisfeito,: From the standpoint of the most dissatisfied group, present in an even smaller fraction of the ratings (~1%), about half complain about the excessive running time and the slow pace of the production. In this same segment, several mention the lack of political depth and historical context, while many point to an excessively heroic approach and the lack of criticism of the central figure.
